correctness.rationale: For the explicit 12-vertex 30-edge icosahedral graph and all real D,h with J>0, all 531441 spin assignments are exhausted and the 49 exact integer bond-minimum sectors reproduced by a separately implemented upper/lower ring contraction. Global inversion covers negative h. Exact rational convex certificates dominate all 30 omitted sectors for every D and h>=0; 19 exact strict positive-field witnesses prove each claimed open chamber. The zero-field 462 and 351 coexistence counts include boundary-only sectors. Both bundled Python standard-library checkers replay successfully. Only finite zero-temperature claims are made.

value.rationale: The highly symmetric icosahedral antiferromagnet is a natural triangularly frustrated finite cluster. Allowing actual zero-spin states produces a nontrivial two-parameter exact 19-region classification with 30 exact dominance certificates, not a one-off numeric slice. The zero-field occupation changes sharply 12 to 8 to 0 at D/J=1/2,1 and exposes otherwise boundary-only occupancy sectors with exact degeneracies 462 and 351. These model-specific coexisting vacancy and frustration patterns are useful in finite-cluster magnetic response and are not just a textbook normalization identity; no thermodynamic extension is asserted.
